# Analysis Plan

## Project Summary
Foldseek.jl currently exposes a single low-level primitive (`foldseek(::Cmd)`) that runs the `Foldseek_jll`-bundled executable. This plan grows it into a Julia wrapper covering the `foldseek` CLI: typed, documented functions for the ~27 commands `foldseek -h` shows (the commands users actually reach for), plus a `foldseek"..."` string macro that passes any command straight through to the CLI verbatim — the escape hatch that gives access to Foldseek's remaining ~150 hidden/inherited commands without needing a typed wrapper for each one. BioJulia ecosystem interop (BioSequences.jl, FASTX.jl, BioAlignments.jl, BioSymbols.jl, MIToS.jl — the protein structure/sequence analysis toolbox at https://github.com/diegozea/MIToS.jl) is an explicit fast-follow, not part of this plan — see Open Questions.

## Language & Environment
- **Language**: Julia 1.10+ (LTS), tested against current release too
- **Key libraries**: `Foldseek_jll` (compat `"10"`); `Test` for the test suite. macOS-only: `Zlib_jll`, `Bzip2_jll`, `LLVMOpenMP_jll`, `Scratch` (see the macOS shadow-executable Working Knowledge entry below for why). No BioJulia deps in this plan.
- **Environment file**: `Project.toml` (already present)
- **Project maturity target**: `releasable-package`
- **Package name(s)**: Foldseek.jl (extending the existing package, not creating a new one)
- **Extending existing package(s)**: Foldseek.jl at `/Users/carlos/git/Foldseek.jl` (this repo)

## Working stance
Intended consumer: reusable lab tool, registry-quality — docstrings, a clean public API, and passing tests are expected in every chunk, not deferred to a polish pass. Off-piste tolerance: default (record adjacent findings in Open Questions rather than pausing or ignoring).

## Target Outputs
No figures/visualization for this plan — the project's outputs are code artifacts and a coverage contract:
- `CLI_NOTES.md` (from CHUNK-001): the full enumerated `foldseek` CLI surface (subcommands + flags), which is the ground truth the rest of the plan is built against.
- A coverage table (in README or `docs/`) mapping every command `foldseek -h` shows to its wrapping Julia function, plus a documented note that `foldseek"..."` covers everything else — the durable evidence that "the whole CLI is reachable from Julia" is met, without requiring a bespoke typed wrapper per command.
- A passing, offline test suite (no network access, no dependence on real research data) — the primary way a future session or collaborator can verify the wrapper still works.
- `scripts/` end-to-end example(s) demonstrating a full workflow through the wrapper alone.

## Working knowledge
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001): `foldseek -h` only shows a curated ~24-command subset. Foldseek is built on the mmseqs2 command framework (`hide_base_commands = true` in `src/foldseek.cpp`) and inherits its full 141-command table, hidden from `-h` but fully callable (confirmed: `foldseek createtsv -h`, `foldseek mvdb -h`, `foldseek version` all work). Several foldseek-specific commands are likewise `COMMAND_HIDDEN` (`version`, `structureto3didescriptor`, `scorecomplex`, ...). Enumerating "the full CLI" requires reading the upstream source command tables (`src/FoldseekBase.cpp`, `lib/mmseqs/src/MMseqsBase.cpp`), not just `-h`. Full inventory and category breakdown in `CLI_NOTES.md`.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001): `BOOL`-typed CLI options (e.g. `-a BOOL`, `--diag-score BOOL`) require an explicit `0`/`1` value passed after the flag — they are not bare presence/absence switches. CHUNK-003's dispatcher must map Julia `Bool` keyword values to `--flag 0`/`--flag 1`, not to a bare `--flag` when true and omitted when false.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001, corrected after user review): whether a command shows up in `foldseek -h` is **not** fully determined by its C++ category — e.g. `structureclusterupdate` is `COMMAND_MAIN` and `lolalign`/`easy-complexsearch` sit in categories that partly appear in `-h`, yet none of the three are actually printed by `foldseek -h`. The literal list of ~27 names printed by `foldseek -h` (recorded verbatim in `CLI_NOTES.md`) is the only reliable ground truth for "is this a typed-wrapper command," not category membership.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001, after user decision): scope for typed wrappers is now fixed at exactly the commands `foldseek -h` prints (~27; see `CLI_NOTES.md`). Everything else — hidden foldseek commands and all inherited mmseqs2 commands — is reached through the `foldseek"..."` string macro (CHUNK-005) instead of individual typed wrappers. This replaces the CHUNK-013 (blocked) / Tier-2 / Tier-3 categorization from the original CHUNK-001 pass; that categorization is superseded, not just deferred.
- 2026-08-16: the string-macro's canonical call syntax is `foldseek"easy-search q.pdb t.pdb out.m8 tmp"` (Julia's `prefix"..."` sugar for a macro named `@foldseek_str`), not `@foldseek"..."` — Julia only expands the `prefix"..."` sugar for macros whose name ends in `_str`; there is no way to make bare `@foldseek"..."` work as a non-standard string literal.
- 2026-08-16 (macOS libomp fix, cross-cutting, not tied to one chunk): the nested-subprocess `libomp.dylib` limitation documented in CHUNK-006/007/008 Notes is now **fixed** on macOS via `src/macos_shadow_executable.jl`. Root cause (confirmed via `otool -l`): `Foldseek_jll`'s macOS artifact has no local `lib/` directory, relying entirely on `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` (injected only for the top-level process); nested re-execs go through `/bin/sh` (SIP-protected, hardened runtime), across which macOS's dyld strips `DYLD_*` env vars. The binary's own `LC_RPATH` is `@loader_path/../lib`, which resolves from the executable's real on-disk location, not any symlink used to invoke it (confirmed empirically — a symlinked shadow binary still fails). The fix: `foldseek(::Cmd)` now runs a real *copy* of the binary cached in `Scratch.jl` space, alongside symlinked `libz.1.dylib`/`libbz2.1.0.dylib`/`libomp.dylib` (exact `@rpath` dependency names, which do **not** always match the JLL-provided on-disk filename — e.g. `Bzip2_jll.libbzip2_path` is `libbz2.1.0.9.dylib` but the binary looks for `libz.1.dylib`/`libbz2.1.0.dylib` exactly). Verified end-to-end: `easy_search`, `search`, `cluster`, and `createsubdb` all now complete successfully against the real fixtures (previously all four aborted). This should make full end-to-end tests possible for CHUNK-009/010's commands too — don't default to bad-flag-only testing without checking first, now that the underlying blocker is gone (this **reverses** the CHUNK-008 Working Knowledge entry telling future chunks to skip empirical checking). An upstream issue against `Foldseek_jll`/Yggdrasil is the durable fix (bundling `lib/` properly would fix this for every consumer, not just this package); tracked as an Open Question until filed.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-006): on this development machine, any Foldseek command that internally re-invokes `foldseek` as a nested subprocess (the `easy-*` commands are embedded shell scripts that do this for each pipeline stage) crashes with a `libomp.dylib` load failure, regardless of whether the given input paths are valid — the top-level process has the right library search path, but it doesn't propagate to the nested re-exec. Single-shot commands with no internal re-exec (`createdb`, confirmed in CHUNK-004) are unaffected. CLI flag validation happens in the top-level process before any internal script runs, so `foldseek <cmd> --bad-flag ...`-style error assertions remain a reliable way to test subcommand/arg-shape correctness even for commands where a full successful run isn't portable to assert on. Expect this to affect any future chunk wrapping a multi-stage workflow command. Full detail in CHUNK-006 Notes.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-008, supersedes the "check each command's -h output" guidance above): the nested-subprocess limitation turned out broader than expected — even `createsubdb`, which looks like a simple single-DB-operation command from its `-h` usage line, generates and runs an internal temp shell script and hits it. `createdb` (direct module, no internal re-exec) is looking like the exception, not the rule. Default assumption for any remaining chunk (009–010): a command is probably not fully runnable in this environment unless there's a specific reason to expect otherwise (e.g. it's a pure format converter with no DB-building step) — don't spend time empirically checking each one before writing tests; go straight to the bad-flag testing strategy and only reach for a real run if it succeeds on the first reasonable attempt.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-005): always pass an output DB path outside `test/data/` (e.g. inside `mktempdir()`) when running `createdb`/similar commands against the fixture files interactively or in tests — with too few positional args, `foldseek` silently treats the last input path as the output prefix and overwrites it in place. Happened once during manual macro testing this session; recovered via `git checkout`. CHUNK-004's own committed smoke test already does this correctly (writes to `mktempdir()`), so this is a note for ad hoc testing, not a fix needed in committed code.
- 2026-08-16 (post-CHUNK-009 fixture addendum): the 1TIM/8TIM fixtures (`createdb`'s `.lookup` groups chains by a 3rd-column complex ID) are already multi-chain complexes — each is a homodimer, chains A and B — but a *homodimer* is the wrong test case for anything exercising heteromeric chain correspondence (`multimersearch`, `multimercluster`, `createmultimerreport`), since chain A and B have identical sequences there. `4hhb.pdb.gz`/`1y8h.pdb.gz` (human/horse hemoglobin, alpha2beta2 tetramers, genuinely distinct alpha/beta chain sequences) were added for that purpose. Before assuming an existing fixture is "monomeric" or "not multimeric" for a future chunk, check its `.lookup` file's complex-ID column rather than assuming from the source PDB filename.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-010): several options across the CLI are short-flag-only, with no `--long-form` equivalent (e.g. `structurealign -a`, "Add backtrace string"). The dispatcher now maps a single-character keyword name to a short `-x` flag rather than `--x`; use e.g. `structurealign(...; a=true)` for these. Multi-character keyword names are unaffected (still `--long-form`).
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-003): the dispatcher's established contract, which every CHUNK-005+ chunk must follow: call `foldseek(subcommand::AbstractString, args::AbstractString...; kwargs...)`; a keyword `foo_bar=value` becomes CLI flag `--foo-bar`; a `Bool` value becomes `"0"`/`"1"`; a keyword value of `nothing` omits that flag entirely — this is how typed wrappers should spell "argument not set" for an optional CLI option. Both `foldseek(::Cmd)` and this method raise a plain `ErrorException` (not `ProcessFailedException`) whose message includes the real stderr text `foldseek` printed.

### CHUNK-001: cli-recon
- **Description**: Run `foldseek -h` to enumerate every module/subcommand, then `foldseek <subcommand> -h` for each to capture its flags, positional arguments, and defaults. Group subcommands by category (database management, easy-workflows, search, clustering, alignment, format conversion, utility/misc). Also inspect what minimal input Foldseek needs (PDB/mmCIF structure requirements) and propose a test-fixture strategy (bundled tiny real structures vs. inline synthetic) for later chunks to use. Write everything to `CLI_NOTES.md`, including a proposed grouping of subcommands into wrapper source files (used to scope CHUNK-005 through CHUNK-008).
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Outputs**: `CLI_NOTES.md`
- **Verification strategy**: Manual review — confirm the subcommand list against `foldseek -h` output and that the grouping is sensible.
- **Notes**: `foldseek -h` covers only ~27 of ~180 total commands; cross-checked the upstream GitHub source (`steineggerlab/foldseek`, shallow-cloned to inspect `FoldseekBase.cpp`/`MMseqsBase.cpp`) to get the authoritative full list, since there's no in-CLI way to list hidden commands. First pass proposed a Tier 1 (wrap now, ~79 commands) / Tier 2 (blocked, ~35 commands) / out-of-scope (~48 commands) split across CHUNK-005–013. After review, the user rejected that in favor of a much narrower scope: typed wrappers only for the exact ~27 commands `foldseek -h` prints, plus a `foldseek"..."` passthrough macro (CHUNK-005) for everything else. Chunks renumbered accordingly below. Test fixture recommendation unchanged: bundle `example/1tim.pdb.gz` + `example/8tim.pdb.gz` from foldseek's own repo (public-domain PDB coordinate data, ~72–84 KB gzipped, two homologous structures giving search/cluster/rbh a genuine positive hit to assert on).

### CHUNK-002: scaffold-package
- **Description**: `Project.toml`, `src/Foldseek.jl`, and `test/runtests.jl` already exist. `Foldseek_jll` is pinned via `compat = "10"`, `julia = "1.10"`. The base primitive `foldseek(args::Cmd)` runs the JLL-bundled executable and returns the `Process`.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: Completed in commit `5a1ecf5` ("Scaffold package: thin wrapper around Foldseek_jll"), prior to this plan's creation.

### CHUNK-003: core-command-dispatcher
- **Description**: Refactor the existing `foldseek(args::Cmd)` primitive into the shared low-level dispatcher every typed subcommand wrapper below (and the CHUNK-005 macro) will call: given a subcommand name, positional args, and Julia keyword arguments, build the corresponding `Cmd` (kwargs map to `--flag value`; per Working Knowledge above, `Bool` values map to `--flag 0`/`--flag 1`, not a bare `--flag`), run it, and raise a Julia error including captured stderr on nonzero exit rather than letting `run` throw its generic `ProcessFailedException`.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001 (flag-naming conventions), CHUNK-002
- **Verification strategy**: Unit tests using argument-free or metadata-only invocations (e.g. `version`, `-h`) that don't require structure data.
- **Notes**: Two-layer design: `foldseek(args::Cmd)` is the primitive (streams stdout live, captures stderr, raises an `ErrorException` with the captured stderr on nonzero exit instead of the less informative `ProcessFailedException`); `foldseek(subcommand::AbstractString, args::AbstractString...; kwargs...)` builds a `Cmd` from a subcommand, positional args, and keyword flags, then calls the `Cmd` method. Keyword keys map `_` → `-` (`comp_bias_corr` → `--comp-bias-corr`); `Bool` values map to `"0"`/`"1"` per the BOOL-flag Working Knowledge entry; a value of `nothing` omits the flag entirely, which is how CHUNK-006+ typed wrappers should represent "unset" optional keyword arguments. Both layers are used by CHUNK-005's macro (via the `Cmd` method) and by every typed wrapper chunk (via the subcommand method). Tests assert on real captured-stderr text from `foldseek createdb` run with missing/bad arguments (`"Not enough input paths"`, `"Unrecognized parameter"`) rather than mocking, since these are stable, documented CLI error messages — no network or structure-file fixtures needed yet.

- **Description**: Based on CHUNK-001's recon, add whatever minimal structure files or synthetic fixtures are needed for database/search/alignment tests, under `test/data/`. If real PDB/mmCIF files are bundled, record their provenance and license in a short note alongside them.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001
- **Verification strategy**: A smoke test that loads/parses each fixture successfully.
- **Notes**: Added `test/data/1tim.pdb.gz` and `test/data/8tim.pdb.gz`, copied unmodified from upstream foldseek's own `example/` directory (commit `21952ed84e0f4a06ec6af08d58add77cef8dec14`); provenance and license rationale in `test/data/PROVENANCE.md`. Smoke test runs `foldseek("createdb", ...)` (CHUNK-003's dispatcher) on both files into a `mktempdir()` output DB and asserts the DB + its index file exist — this exercises the dispatcher against a real multi-step, real-binary invocation for the first time, not just metadata-only commands. Note: `createdb` reports "Ignore 4 out of 8. Too short: 4" — of the two files' combined chains, 4 are filtered out as too short; this doesn't fail the command and isn't a fixture problem, just expected chain-filtering on these particular structures.
  - 2026-08-16 addendum (post-CHUNK-009, user-requested): 1TIM/8TIM turned out to be homodimers, not adequate for exercising genuinely heteromeric complexes (distinct chain types) in `multimersearch`/`multimercluster`/`createmultimerreport`. Added `test/data/4hhb.pdb.gz` (human deoxyhemoglobin, alpha2beta2) and `test/data/1y8h.pdb.gz` (horse methemoglobin, same architecture), downloaded directly from RCSB — provenance in `test/data/PROVENANCE.md`. Used to upgrade those three commands' tests from bad-flag-only to real end-to-end runs (see CHUNK-007 and CHUNK-009 Notes).

### CHUNK-005: foldseek-str-macro
- **Description**: A `@foldseek_str` macro (used as `foldseek"easy-search q.pdb t.pdb out.m8 tmp"`) that tokenizes its string argument the way a shell would (quoting/escaping included — reuse `Base.shell_split`, the same tokenizer Julia's own `` `cmd` `` literal uses internally) and runs it through CHUNK-003's dispatcher. This is the universal escape hatch: any command not covered by a typed wrapper (CHUNK-006 onward), including every hidden foldseek command and all ~141 commands inherited from mmseqs2, stays reachable without writing a bespoke wrapper for each one. High priority — this is what makes the narrower CHUNK-006+ scope (typed wrappers only for `foldseek -h` commands) acceptable rather than a coverage gap.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003
- **Verification strategy**: Unit tests comparing `foldseek"version"`-style invocations (and a case with a quoted argument containing a space) against the equivalent direct dispatcher call.
- **Notes**: Implemented as `macro foldseek_str(s)` that tokenizes `s` with `Base.shell_split` at macro-expansion time and splices the resulting `Vector{String}` into a call to `foldseek(::Cmd)` (CHUNK-003's primitive) — so tokenizing happens once per call site, not once per invocation. Confirmed (docstring note + test): unlike `` `cmd` `` backtick literals, custom string macros in Julia do **not** get `$`-interpolation of Julia values — only the built-in backtick syntax gets that special parser treatment. Users needing dynamic values should build a `Cmd` or use the `foldseek(subcommand, args...; kwargs...)` method instead. Quoting correctness (a quoted, space-containing argument surviving as one token) is tested by asserting on the specific stderr text a correct vs. incorrect split would produce, not by inspecting tokens directly. One process-note, not a package issue: manually testing the macro against the CHUNK-004 fixtures without an explicit distinct output path caused `foldseek` to treat `test/data/8tim.pdb.gz` itself as the output DB prefix and overwrite it in the working tree; recovered with `git checkout -- test/data/8tim.pdb.gz` plus deleting the generated sidecar files. No code or fixture change resulted — flagging so a future session doesn't repeat it uncommitted.

### CHUNK-006: easy-workflow-commands
- **Description**: Typed wrappers for the 5 "Easy workflows" commands `foldseek -h` prints: `easy-search`, `easy-cluster`, `easy-rbh`, `easy-multimercluster`, `easy-multimersearch`. These are the most commonly used entry points (single-call structure search/clustering without manual DB management) — prioritize getting these right.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003, CHUNK-004
- **Notes**: Added `src/easy_workflows.jl` (included from `src/Foldseek.jl`) with one function per command. Each `queryfiles`-taking command has two methods: one for `AbstractVector{<:AbstractString}` (the real implementation) and a convenience one for a single `AbstractString` that wraps it in a vector — `easy-rbh` is the one command in this group that takes exactly one query file per the CLI itself, so it has no vector method. Positional argument order in each function matches its `-h` usage line exactly (transcribed in `CLI_NOTES.md`); every other CLI option is exposed generically through `kwargs...` rather than declared individually — these commands have 60-90+ flags each, and hand-declaring each one would duplicate documentation that already exists in `foldseek <cmd> -h` and would drift on every Foldseek version bump. This generic-kwargs pattern is the model for every remaining typed-wrapper chunk (CHUNK-007–010), not just this one.

  **Environment finding, not a code defect**: on this development machine (macOS/Apple Silicon), running any `easy-*` command against real data crashes with a `Library not loaded: .../libomp.dylib` error from a *nested* `foldseek` subprocess these commands spawn internally (they're implemented as embedded shell scripts, e.g. `easystructuresearch.sh`, that re-invoke `foldseek` as `$MMSEQS createdb ...` for each pipeline stage). The top-level process has the correct library search path (confirmed: `foldseek(::Cmd)` and CHUNK-004's `createdb` test both work), but that environment doesn't propagate to the nested re-exec. This happens regardless of whether the given input paths are valid, so it isn't reachable/avoidable from wrapper code and isn't specific to any one command's arguments. CLI-level flag validation (`Unrecognized parameter ...`) happens in the top-level process *before* the internal script runs, so it's unaffected and gives a reliable, environment-independent way to test subcommand routing and positional-arg shape — used for all 9 test cases in this chunk. A true end-to-end run of any `easy-*` command should still be tried against real data on whatever machine ends up using this package; if it works there, this note can be narrowed to "confirmed on macOS/arm64 with Foldseek_jll v10" rather than treated as universal.

- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003, CHUNK-004
- **Notes**: Added `src/main_workflows.jl`. Function names map 1:1 to CLI subcommand names (`createdb`, `search`, `rbh`, `cluster`, `multimercluster`, `multimersearch`), same convention as CHUNK-006. `createdb` is the one variadic-input command here (multiple files/dirs/tar/DB → single output DB, same shape as before); the other five take fixed-count DB-path arguments (they operate on databases `createdb` already built, not raw structure files — that's the actual distinction between "Easy workflows" and "Main workflows" in `-h`'s own grouping). Confirmed empirically (not assumed) that `search` and `cluster` are also internal shell-script workflows that hit the same nested-subprocess `libomp.dylib` issue as CHUNK-006's `easy-*` commands; `rbh`, `multimercluster`, `multimersearch` are presumed to be the same pattern (same "Main workflows" category, not verified individually) and tested the same way — bad-flag assertions rather than full runs. `createdb`, being a direct module with no internal re-exec, gets full end-to-end tests against the real fixtures instead, through both its single-path and vector-of-paths methods.
  - 2026-08-16 addendum (post-CHUNK-009, user-requested): `multimersearch` and `multimercluster` upgraded to real end-to-end tests using the new `4hhb.pdb.gz`/`1y8h.pdb.gz` heteromeric hemoglobin fixtures (see CHUNK-004 addendum) — both were fully runnable (no libomp issue), confirming the "presumed same pattern" note above was right about the crash mode but the underlying macOS fix already covers them. `rbh` remains untested beyond flag validation — no rbh-specific fixture need identified.

  **Naming collision risk, flagged not fixed**: `search`, `rbh`, and `cluster` are short, generic exported names with real collision potential if a user does `using Foldseek` alongside another package that also exports `search` or `cluster` (Julia will require qualification, not silently misresolve — but it's friction). Chose to keep the direct 1:1 CLI-name mapping anyway, for consistency with CHUNK-006 and because it's what makes the API predictable to someone who already knows the `foldseek` CLI. Revisit if this becomes an actual reported problem — renaming later is non-breaking at this stage (package not yet released).

### CHUNK-009: format-conversion-commands
- **Description**: Typed wrappers for the 4 "Format conversion" commands `foldseek -h` prints: `convertalis`, `compressca`, `convert2pdb`, `createmultimerreport`. Parse `convertalis`'s tabular output into a native Julia structure (`Vector` of `NamedTuple`s) rather than leaving it as raw text.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-007
- **Notes**: Added `src/format_conversion.jl`. `convertalis` runs the CLI command (writing the alignment file as always) and then parses that file into a `Vector` of `NamedTuple`s: the column set comes from the `format_output` kwarg if given, else `foldseek`'s own default column list; each field is coerced `Int` → `Float64` → `String` by trial parsing rather than hardcoding types for the ~60 possible output columns (same drift-avoidance rationale as the generic-kwargs pattern from CHUNK-006). A row whose field count doesn't match the expected column count raises an error instead of silently mis-zipping fields — this only supports the default tabular `--format-mode` (0); SAM/HTML/PDB modes aren't parseable this way and aren't handled. Empirically confirmed (not assumed) that `convertalis`, `compressca`, and `convert2pdb` are direct modules with no internal re-exec, so all three get full end-to-end tests against the real fixtures (a `search` result for `convertalis`, `createdb` output for the other two) — consistent with the now-fixed macOS libomp issue making real runs the default expectation again. `createmultimerreport` needs a multimer-level complex DB (e.g. from `multimersearch`), which the monomeric 1TIM/8TIM fixtures can't produce, so it's tested via flag validation only, same as the other untested commands in earlier chunks.
  - 2026-08-16 addendum (user-requested): `createmultimerreport` upgraded to a real end-to-end test using the new `4hhb.pdb.gz`/`1y8h.pdb.gz` heteromeric fixtures and a `multimersearch` result (see CHUNK-004/CHUNK-007 addenda) — fully runnable, 4 chain-permutation rows each with TM-score > 0.8.

- **Notes**: Added `src/alignment_commands.jl`. All 8 operate on an intermediate pipeline DB (a prefilter or alignment result) rather than a raw structure DB, so testing them meant building that input directly through the untyped `prefilter` command (`foldseek("prefilter", ...)` — no typed wrapper, it's one of the ~150 commands out of scope per the CHUNK-001 scope decision). All 8 turned out to be direct modules with no internal re-exec and are fully tested end to end: `tmalign`/`structurealign`/`structurerescorediagonal` via `convertalis`-parsed rows (TM-score/fident > 0.9 on the 1TIM/8TIM pair), `clust` via the hidden `createtsv` command (confirms all 4 chains land in one cluster), `expandmultimer`/`scoremultimer` by hand-reconstructing the internal pipeline `multimersearch` normally runs automatically (prefilter → structurealign → expandmultimer → structurealign -a 1 → scoremultimer) against the heteromeric 4HHB/1Y8H pair and checking the resulting `createmultimerreport` output matches `multimersearch`'s own end-to-end result from CHUNK-007/009. `aln2tmscore` and `result2profile` are checked by file existence only — their output DB types aren't `convertalis`-readable.

  **Dispatcher fix, not scoped to this chunk but discovered here**: `structurealign`'s `-a` (add backtrace) flag has no `--long-form` equivalent, which the CHUNK-003 dispatcher couldn't reach — it only ever emitted `--flag`. Fixed `foldseek(subcommand, args...; kwargs...)` in `src/Foldseek.jl` so a single-character keyword name maps to a short `-x` flag instead, matching Foldseek's own convention that every short option is exactly one letter. Backward compatible (no existing kwarg name was a single character); added a dedicated dispatcher-level test (`foldseek("version"; v=1)`).

### CHUNK-011: public-api-and-docs
- **Description**: Consolidate module exports, write docstrings for every exported symbol (including `@foldseek_str`), and produce the coverage table (README or `docs/`) mapping each `foldseek -h` command to its Julia function, with a note documenting `foldseek"..."` as the path to every other command.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-005, CHUNK-006, CHUNK-007, CHUNK-008, CHUNK-009, CHUNK-010
- **Notes**: Audited rather than rewritten — every exported symbol already had a docstring from its own chunk, verified programmatically (`haskey(Base.Docs.meta(Foldseek), Docs.Binding(Foldseek, name))` for all 29 exported names). Added a module-level docstring to `src/Foldseek.jl` (a docstring immediately before `module Foldseek`); confirmed it's correctly stored in the docs metadata (`Docs.meta(Foldseek)` has the `Foldseek.Foldseek` binding) even though bare `@doc Foldseek` returns `nothing` in non-interactive `julia -e` batch mode — a known Julia quirk with self-referencing module bindings outside the REPL's doc-system bootstrap, not a defect in the docstring itself. Rewrote `README.md` (previously a two-line stub) with installation, a quick-start example, and a full command coverage table — 27 rows, one per `foldseek -h` command, grouped exactly as `-h` itself groups them (cross-checked programmatically: the table's function names minus `foldseek`/`@foldseek_str` exactly equal `Foldseek`'s other exported names). Used plain `` `code` `` spans for function names in the README table rather than `[`name`](@ref)`-style links — those only resolve under Documenter.jl, which this project doesn't have set up (no `docs/` build), so they'd render as broken links in GitHub's plain markdown rendering; `(@ref)` links remain appropriate inside docstrings themselves (an established convention already used throughout this codebase, since Julia's REPL help mode renders that markdown reasonably even without Documenter).
